currentCard.prompt: Как называется переход снега или льда прямо в водяной пар?

answers.note: Кальвинг — отделение глыб льда от фронта ледника или шельфа.
В очень сухих районах Антарктиды сублимация может приводить к исчезновению ледников.
Фирнизация превращает многолетний снег в зернистый фирн, а затем в ледниковый лёд.
Абляция — совокупная потеря массы ледником из-за таяния, испарения и откалывания.

sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.individualGround: Direct solid snow/ice to gas is specifically sublimation, stated atGlacierL67. Four real glacier/ice-process names are comparable distractors: solid chunks detach in calving; snow densifies in firn formation; ablation is broader mass removal, which can encompass several loss mechanisms rather than the exact phase-change name. The presence of an umbrella term does not create a second equally specific name for the direct solid-to-vapor transition.

sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.individualGround: Directly names сублимация in first sentence. Direct solid-to-gas conversion removes material without a liquid meltwater stage; this is the exactphysical consequence ofL67. It does not claim every glacier loses mass only this way or that no melting occurs elsewhere on the same glacier.

В очень сухих районах and может preserve non-universal conditions; not allAntarctica/allglaciers extinction.

sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.literal: Фирнизация превращает многолетний снег в зернистый фирн, а затем в ледниковый лёд.
sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.individualGround: Snow surviving melt season becomes denser firn and subsequent overburden compaction joins buried layers into glacier ice atL72-L74. Russian sentence describes firnification within that snow-to-firn-to-ice sequence; it does not present solid-to-gas loss. A useful own definition for this distractor.

sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.literal: Абляция — совокупная потеря массы ледником из-за таяния, испарения и откалывания.
sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.individualGround: Broad glacier mass loss includes melting/evaporation/calving as described together atL72 andretreatL84; ablation areaL108 explicitly covers melting/evaporation. This is a scientific synthesis of those contexts rather than a claimed verbatim three-item dictionary quote; the list does not say these are the only mechanisms. It distinguishes an umbrella loss concept from the specific solid-to-gas name.
